From e38c55d9f834e5b848bfed0f5c586aaf45acb825 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Massimiliano Pellizzer <massimiliano.pellizzer@canonical.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 15:24:04 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] apparmor: fix memory leak in verify_header

The function sets `*ns = NULL` on every call, leaking the namespace
string allocated in previous iterations when multiple profiles are
unpacked. This also breaks namespace consistency checking since *ns
is always NULL when the comparison is made.

Remove the incorrect assignment.
The caller (aa_unpack) initializes *ns to NULL once before the loop,
which is sufficient.

Fixes: dd51c8485763 ("apparmor: provide base for multiple profiles to be replaced at once")
Reported-by: Qualys Security Advisory <qsa@qualys.com>
Tested-by: Salvatore Bonaccorso <carnil@debian.org>
Reviewed-by: Georgia Garcia <georgia.garcia@canonical.com>
Reviewed-by: Cengiz Can <cengiz.can@canonical.com>
Signed-off-by: Massimiliano Pellizzer <massimiliano.pellizzer@canonical.com>
Signed-off-by: John Johansen <john.johansen@canonical.com>

diff --git a/security/apparmor/policy_unpack.c b/security/apparmor/policy_unpack.c
index ba5d40dbeb24..5d90ea55de82 100644
--- a/security/apparmor/policy_unpack.c
+++ b/security/apparmor/policy_unpack.c
@@ -1419,7 +1419,6 @@ static int verify_header(struct aa_ext *e, int required, const char **ns)
 {
 	int error = -EPROTONOSUPPORT;
 	const char *name = NULL;
-	*ns = NULL;
 
 	/* get the interface version */
 	if (!aa_unpack_u32(e, &e->version, "version")) {
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file:

- **`security/apparmor/policy_unpack.c`**: Removed the line `*ns = NULL;` in the `verify_header` function.

**Relationship**: The removed assignment was erroneous because `verify_header` is called within a loop in `aa_unpack` (the caller). The caller initializes `*ns` to `NULL` once before the loop, which is sufficient. By setting `*ns = NULL` on every call, the function leaked the namespace string allocated in previous iterations and broke namespace consistency checking (since `*ns` was always `NULL` when compared). The fix restores proper behavior without reintroducing the leak.

Reason:
This assignment resets the namespace pointer to NULL on every call to `verify_header`, causing memory leaks of previously allocated namespace strings and preventing correct namespace consistency checking because `*ns` is always NULL when the comparison is made.

The code statements that fix the bug are:

Reason:
Removing this assignment ensures that the namespace pointer is only initialized once by the caller (`aa_unpack`) before the loop, allowing proper memory management and namespace consistency verification.
